title: Amazon RDS Fundamentals
description: Learn to provision and manage relational databases on AWS using Amazon RDS, including engines, Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and security.

data.text: Amazon RDS makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale relational databases in the cloud. Instead of installing and managing database software yourself, AWS handles the heavy lifting — backups, patches, and hardware failures.
RDS supports six popular database engines. Each engine is a different flavor of relational database, and you choose the one that matches your application's needs.

data.title: RDS Database Engines
items: **Amazon Aurora** — AWS's cloud-native database, compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL
**MySQL** — the world's most popular open-source relational database
**PostgreSQL** — advanced open-source database known for reliability and feature set
**MariaDB** — community-developed fork of MySQL with additional features
**Oracle** — enterprise-grade commercial database for complex workloads
**SQL Server** — Microsoft's relational database for Windows-based applications

data.text: A Multi-AZ deployment automatically creates a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone. If the primary database fails, RDS promotes the standby to primary in about 60-120 seconds with no manual intervention.

data.title: Production Best Practice
data.text: Always use Multi-AZ for production databases. The automatic failover keeps your application running during AZ outages.

Read replicas are asynchronous copies of your primary database. They are great for scaling read-heavy workloads. You can have up to 15 read replicas for a single primary database (5 for SQL Server and Oracle).

RDS automatically backs up your database daily and stores transaction logs every 5 minutes. You can restore to any point in time within your retention period (up to 35 days). DB parameter groups let you customize database settings for your engine.

RDS integrates with AWS IAM for authentication. You can also encrypt data at rest using AWS KMS and encrypt data in transit using SSL/TLS. Security groups act as a firewall to control access to your database.

data.title: Create an RDS MySQL Instance with AWS CLI
data.content: Run this command in your terminal to create a MySQL RDS instance. Replace the placeholder values with your own.
data.code:
aws rds create-db-instance \
  --db-instance-identifier my-mysql-db \
  --db-instance-class db.t3.micro \
  --engine mysql \
  --engine-version 8.0 \
  --master-username admin \
  --master-user-password MySecurePassword123 \
  --allocated-storage 20 \
  --storage-type gp3 \
  --multi-az \
  --no-publicly-accessible \
  --backup-retention-period 7

terms.definition: An isolated database environment running in the cloud. Each instance has its own compute, memory, and storage.
A deployment that automatically creates a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone for high availability.
An asynchronous copy of a primary database used to offload read traffic and scale read performance.
A container for database engine configuration values that can be applied to one or more DB instances.
A virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic to your RDS instance.

data.title: Create and Connect to an RDS Instance
data.description: Create a free-tier eligible RDS MySQL instance in the AWS console, then connect to it using the MySQL command-line client.
steps: Open the RDS console and click 'Create database'
Choose 'Standard Create' and select MySQL engine
Set a master username and password
Connect to the instance endpoint using the MySQL client
data.expectedOutcome: You should see the MySQL prompt connected to your RDS instance. You can now run SQL queries.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RDS manages backups, patches, and failover for six database engines
Multi-AZ provides automatic failover for high availability
Use IAM, KMS encryption, and security groups to secure your database
data.takeaway: RDS removes the operational burden of running relational databases so you can focus on your application.
